title: TIME JUMP: Shock Arrival, 13:24 CDT

fields.narration: THIS IS AN EXERCISE. The exercise clock is now 03:00, one hour after STARTEX. The story jumps to Tuesday afternoon, 16 March 2027, at 13:24 CDT. The Kp has stayed at 3 since the noon news. Day load has risen to 2,860 MW. Arrowhead imports are 780 MW against the 1,000 MW limit, and North Shore imports are 470 MW against 600 MW. The control room alarm has just sounded for an SWPC message that starts with WARSUD. On the screen: '*** EXERCISE *** Space Weather Message Code: WARSUD, Serial Number: 0412, Issue Time: 2027 Mar 16 1824 UTC. WARNING: Geomagnetic Sudden Impulse expected. Valid From: 2027 Mar 16 1835 UTC, Valid To: 2027 Mar 16 1905 UTC. IP Shock Passage Observed: 2027 Mar 16 1817 UTC. Expected Amplitude: 45 nT. *** EXERCISE ***' Solar wind speed at L1 jumped from 410 to 890 kilometres per second in one sample. The EMS GIC display goes up with every 10-second scan: Iron Range AT-2 neutral at 31 amps, Hartley AT-1 at 22 amps, Cloquet AT-1 at 18 amps. From now on the shift has to keep up with the storm itself, not the forecast.
worldState: Time is 13:24 CDT / 1824 UTC, Tuesday 16 March 2027. The CME has arrived at L1: the shock passed at 1817 UTC (13:17 CDT), inside the 1600–2200 UTC arrival window.
SWPC WARSUD serial 0412, issued 1824 UTC, is valid 1835–1905 UTC (13:35–14:05 CDT), with an expected amplitude of 45 nT. It has not been logged yet.
L1 solar wind speed is 890 km/s, up from 410 km/s. The real-time Kp estimate still reads 3 because it has not caught up with the shock yet.
System load is 2,860 MW. Arrowhead imports are 780 MW of 1,000 MW and North Shore imports are 470 MW of 600 MW.
GIC neutral currents are rising: IRON_RANGE_AT2_GIC_NEUT 31 A, HARTLEY_AT1 22 A, CLOQUET_AT1 18 A. All are below 75 A, and all are trending up.
All decisions made earlier in the day still stand as taken: the planned outages, the Hartley AT-1 crew, the GPS clock firmware push, the reactive resources and the public messages.
On the UMRC Notification System the RC level is still Alert. No GMD Warning has gone out to TOPs, generator owners or neighbors yet.
Day shift on desk: Control Room Shift Supervisor Walter Nakamura. UMRC Shift Manager on duty: Hugo Villanueva.
fields.facilitatorNote: WARSUD is a sudden-impulse trigger for NGDOP 4 Condition 2 and for the UMRC Warning level in UGFNWC 4. The RC's 15-minute dissemination clock runs from 1824 UTC, so the Warning is due by 13:39 CDT. Watch whether the CRSS logs the code, serial and both UTC and Central times, and whether the RE starts trending neutral currents against the 75 A Condition 3 trigger.
fields.scenarioTitle: Aurora Over Texas — GIC, Conservative Operations & Timing Holdover

instructorNote: This card moves the scenario from forecast to arrival. The sudden impulse should start Condition 2 actions, if they are not already done, and the RC GMD Warning to the TOP, generator owner and neighbor lists by 13:39 CDT. The Warning should carry the serial number, UTC and Central times, a duration of several hours to a day, and the next hourly bridge call. Watch whether the CRSS logs WARSUD 0412 correctly, whether the 14 entities are notified, and whether the RE begins trending GIC against the 75 A trigger.
